title: What If Every Cow on Earth Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every cow vanished tonight? The climate would notice first.
Livestock cause about 14.5 percent of human-made greenhouse gases, and cattle make up roughly two thirds of that.
That's about a tenth of all emissions. Nearly half of the livestock total is methane.
Methane is short-lived, lasting roughly a dozen years in the air, so warming from it would ease within a decade or two.
But the cost would be huge. Livestock provide around a third of the protein people eat, and beef and milk would be gone overnight.
Grasslands would change too. Without grazers, many pastures would slowly turn to scrub or forest.

description:
What if every cow vanished?
About a tenth of human-made emissions would stop, but a huge share of the world's protein would go with them.
